newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds open firmer, following U.S..
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds open firmer, following U.S..

text.p: Canadian bonds opened slightly firmer on Thursday on the back of the U.S. market as investors seemed to believe that they had consolidated enough after Tuesday's rally.

"It comes from the U.S. market and Canada is just feeding off it," said Toronto-Dominion Securities analyst Arve Bendiksrud. North American bonds rallied on Tuesday, boosted by bullish economic remarks by U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan, but slipped afterward on profit-taking.
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond rose C$0.07 to C$120.23 to yield 6.461 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond gained 10/32 to yield 6.41 percent and the spread between the bonds widened to five basis points from three at Wednesday's close.
Technical Data analyst David Ebata said the market was still trying to distribute yesterday's supply from the 30-year C$1.3 billion bond auction.

New corporate bonds have also been flooding the market, analysts noted. The Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce set a US$250 million 15-year floating-rate issue early on Thursday and the Canadian Mortgage and Housing Corp set C$200 million of 5.5 percent bonds due 2002 on Thursday.
The short end of the curve remained under pressure because many market players expect the Bank of Canada to increase short-term interest rates to prop up a sinking dollar, Ebata added.

In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond fell C$0.03 to reach C$109.79 to yield 5.909 percent. The U.S. 10-year bond rose 2/32 to yield 6.14 percent, so the negative spread between the bonds stayed steady at 23 basis points from Wednesday's close.
